description: Ornamental evergreen tree of 3 to 10 metres, with fragrant white flowers and ribbed red to orange berries. The fruit is sweet-tart and strongly aromatic.
nativeStatus: Native to northeastern Argentina and the broader subtropical Río de la Plata region
ecology: Wild birds disperse the seed by eating the fruit, which is how it spreads through subtropical woodland.
wildlifeNotes: Birds eat and disperse the fruit. The fragrant white flowers draw pollinators.
size: Altura / height: 3-10 m. Porte: árbol frutal pequeño, perenne, de copa redondeada.
propagation: Prefers some shelter while establishing. Once established it handles Buenos Aires cold well.
edibleUses: Sweet-tart and aromatic, loaded with lycopene, anthocyanins and vitamin C. Eat fresh, or use for jam, liqueur or ice cream.
medicinalUses: In Brazilian folk medicine the leaf tea is taken for diarrhoea, fever and high blood pressure. It carries significant antioxidant and antimicrobial activity.
sources: Árboles nativos, Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires: https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/arboles-nativos/nangapiri | Árboles nativos de Argentina, Argentina Forestal: https://www.argentinaforestal.com/2026/04/29/arboles-nativos-de-argentina/
notes: Ya tenemos uno en el santuario. / Already in the sanctuary.
